World English Bible (Catholic), eBible.org, https://ebible.org/eng-web-c/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this translation, https://ebible.org/eng-web-c/copyright.htm):
> Catholic Book Order
> The World English Bible is in the Public Domain. That means that it is not copyrighted. However, "World English Bible" is a Trademark of eBible.org.
> You may copy, publish, proclaim, distribute, redistribute, sell, give away, quote, memorize, read publicly, broadcast, transmit, share, back up, post on the Internet, print, reproduce, preach, teach from, and use
> the World English Bible as much as you want, and others may also do so. All we ask is that if you CHANGE the actual text of the World English Bible in any way, you not call the result the World English Bible any more.
> This is to avoid confusion, not to limit your freedom. The Holy Bible is God's Word. It belongs to God. He gave it to us freely, and we who have worked on this translation freely give it to you by dedicating it to the
> Public Domain.
> Donations to help with the expenses of this project and thus help others have free access to the Word of God may be made to us, but are not required. Please see
> https://MLJohnson.org/partner/ for more about that.
> Although we are done with the editing for language updates, we might choose to consider corrections of obvious typos or problems in the translation.
> Any updates will be posted on https://eBible.org/web/ and at https://WorldEnglish.Bible.
> 2020 stable text edition

Why this is public domain:
Text: the World English Bible in Catholic book order, with Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch, Maccabees and Greek Esther and Daniel. Editor and main translator: Michael Paul Johnson (living, United States), who is also the owner of eBible.org (WEB FAQ: "The senior editor and main translator is Michael Paul Johnson"; eBible.org's legal page names eBible.org a registered business name running mljohnson.org and WorldEnglish.Bible). The other contributors are not listed (WEB FAQ: "We don't publish a complete list"); the project's dedication covers them. Base text: the American Standard Version, first published in 1901 in the United States, public domain there since it was published before 1931. Its deuterocanonical books come from the Apocrypha of the Revised Version (Oxford and Cambridge University Presses, preface dated January 1895, United Kingdom), whose preface names its revisers, so the life-plus-70 rule applies to each: Charles John Ellicott 1819-1905, George Moberly 1803-1885, Robert Scott 1811-1887, Edward Bickersteth 1814-1892, Joseph Angus 1816-1902, William Gilson Humphry 1815-1886, Richard Chenevix Trench 1807-1886, Arthur Penrhyn Stanley 1815-1881, Edwin Palmer 1824-1895, F. H. A. Scrivener 1813-1891, J. B. Lightfoot 1828-1889, Joseph Williams Blakesley 1808-1885, F. J. A. Hort 1828-1892, B. F. Westcott 1825-1901, William Fiddian Moulton 1835-1898, John Troutbeck 1832-1899, J. J. S. Perowne 1823-1904, J. Rawson Lumby 1831-1895, William Robertson Smith 1846-1894, Robert Lubbock Bensly 1831-1893, T. K. Cheyne 1841-1915, William Aldis Wright 1831-1914, Frederick Field 1801-1885, Charles Wordsworth 1806-1892, Charles John Vaughan 1816-1897, David Brown 1803-1897, Samuel Newth 1821-1898, George Vance Smith 1816-1902, William Milligan 1821-1893, Benjamin Hall Kennedy 1804-1889, Alexander Roberts 1826-1901, William Lee 1815-1883. The last of them died in 1915, so the United Kingdom's life plus 70 years ended in 1985; published in 1895, it is public domain in the United States. Parts not in the Revised Version Apocrypha come from Brenton's Septuagint (Brenton died 1862). The maintainer's rule (2026-10-16): a translation project's own public-domain dedication, in the project's own words and contradicted by nothing from the same holder, counts as the authors' own. The statement asks that a changed text not be called by the translation's name, "a condition of our trademark use" (WEB FAQ). The maintainer's decision (2026-10-16): this restricts only the name, not copying or changing the text, so it does not contradict the dedication.

The verse-per-line archive holds the Bible text in one file, one verse per line, each line starting with its reference (book, chapter:verse); its SQL and XML copies of the same text, eBible.org's description page, style sheet and signature are left out of the source.

Sources of these facts: eBible.org's details page (https://ebible.org/details.php?id=eng-web-c), the edition's copyright page (https://ebible.org/eng-web-c/copyright.htm), https://ebible.org/eng-web/webfaq.htm; https://ebible.org/legal.php; https://worldenglish.bible/; the Revised Version Apocrypha (https://archive.org/details/apocryphatransla00oxfo); life dates from the English Wikipedia page of each reviser and Wikidata (Q8009009, Q7347030, Q5079548, Q5341885, Q18672905, Q5346735, Q5231795, Q18734771, Q18954224, Q8015646, Q4219395, Q15627347, Q5083718); https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1988/48/section/12; https://copyright.cornell.edu/publicdomain.

note: The verse-numbered twin of ebible-eng-web-c-1fd762ff, for the parallel verses measure only (#35): its tag is verse-numbers alone, which no mixture selects, so it never enters training. eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside.
